scenes.title: 1974 Seattle lecture room: 'smashed' vs 'hit' questionnaires plant phantom broken glass on a clean crash film
scenes.era: 1974, University of Washington psychology screening classroom, Seattle

layout.description: Bright 1970s university screening room with a 16mm film projector casting a two-car intersection bump onto a white pull-down screen (clean asphalt, zero shattered glass); at wooden student desks in front, undergraduates fill out printed questionnaires where one sheet reads 'SMASHED' and another reads 'CONTACTED', while Elizabeth Loftus stands beside the projector holding the week-two 'broken glass' tally.

positions.who: Elizabeth Loftus (mannequin in 1970s tailored blazer and wide-collar blouse)
positions.where: standing beside the 16mm projector and pull-down screen holding two contrasting question sheets

positions.who: Student witness A ('smashed' condition mannequin in 1970s sweater)
positions.where: seated front-left writing '41 mph' and checking 'YES — broken glass' on a printed form
positions.facing: facing the paper questionnaire and screen

positions.who: Student witness B ('contacted' condition mannequin in denim jacket)
positions.where: seated front-right writing '32 mph' and checking 'NO' on the matching form

props.name: 16mm classroom film projector and pull-down screen
props.period_detail: brushed-metal 1970s Bell & Howell 16mm reel projector showing two sedans bumping cleanly on spotless pavement
props.physical_behavior: projector beam illuminates the clean road with zero glass

props.name: two printed survey sheets ('SMASHED' vs 'CONTACTED')
props.period_detail: crisp white 1974 typed questionnaires differing by only one bolded verb
props.physical_behavior: ballpoint pen checks the 'Yes, saw broken glass' box on the 'smashed' sheet

props.name: week-later calendar flip stand
props.period_detail: desktop calendar flipped forward seven days to Day 8
props.physical_behavior: marks the one-week delay before the broken-glass test

actions.verb_sequence: clicks off the 16mm crash film -> hands the 'smashed' sheet left and 'contacted' sheet right
reads the word 'smashed' -> writes a fast speed estimate -> checks 'YES' to seeing broken glass that never existed

reactions.reaction: nods with total certainty in his false recollection
holds up both completed forms showing the 32% vs 14% phantom-glass split

scenes.wardrobe: 1974 collegiate knit sweaters, corduroy jackets, and wide-lapel blazer on Loftus.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key classroom daylight balanced with the bright 16mm projection screen.
scenes.recognition_hook: Watchers of the exact same clean fender-bender film checked 'Yes, I saw broken glass' twice as often just because one question used the word 'smashed.'

key_visual.description: students in a 1974 screening room watch a clean car-bump film on a projector screen and check yes to broken glass on a smashed questionnaire

scenes.title: 1995 'Lost in the Mall' family booklet interview

layout.description: Quiet sunlit interview office where a young adult reads a four-event childhood booklet and begins gesturing to describe details of a fictional mall rescue.

positions.where: seated in an armchair holding the typed childhood memory booklet
positions.facing: gesturing vividly as they 'recall' the elderly rescuer

positions.where: seated across a small table taking notes

props.name: four-story childhood booklet
props.period_detail: stapled white booklet containing three real family stories and one fabricated age-five mall story
props.physical_behavior: participant turns to Story #3 and nods in recognition

actions.verb_sequence: reads the planted paragraph -> looks up and gestures to describe the rescuer's flannel shirt

reactions.reaction: records how 25 percent embellished a day that never happened

scenes.recognition_hook: One in four adults read a fake paragraph about getting lost in a mall at age five and started remembering what the rescuer wore.

scenes.title: Open-ended vs leading police witness interview reform

layout.description: Clean modern interview room comparing a leading interviewer pointing suggestively versus an open-ended neutral notepad protocol.

positions.where: seated at an interview table recalling calmly without interruption
seated with hands resting neutrally beside an open-question checklist

props.period_detail: numbered manila folders handed by an officer who does not know which photo is the suspect

actions.verb_sequence: slides numbered folders across the table and steps back neutrally

scenes.recognition_hook: Double-blind lineups and open questions grew directly out of Loftus's misinformation research.
